chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abī Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who said to another man, 'Write, O so-and-so, to my wife regarding her divorce,' or said, 'Write to my slave regarding his emancipation.' Would that constitute divorce or emancipation?

He عليه السلام said: 'There is no divorce and no emancipation until the tongue utters it or he writes it with his own hand while intending divorce or emancipation, and that is done by him with the proper times and witnesses, while he is absent from his family.'

key_terms.طَلَاقِهَا: her divorce; the legal dissolution of marriage
key_terms.عِتْقِهِ: his emancipation; the freeing of a slave
key_terms.غَائِبًا: absent; not present with his family
key_terms.يَخُطَّ: to write by hand; to inscribe personally
key_terms.يَنْطِقَ: to pronounce verbally; to utter the formula by speech
key_terms.يُرِيدُ: to intend; to possess the deliberate legal intention

ai.seo_question: Does telling someone else to write a divorce or emancipation count as a valid legal act in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that divorce and emancipation are not established merely by instructing another person to write them. They require direct utterance or personal writing accompanied by intention, along with the applicable formal conditions such as witnesses and the circumstance of absence from one's family.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4766 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbub narrated from Abu Ḥamzah al-Thumali from Abu Jafar Imam Al-Baqir (as) who said:
"I asked him about a man who said to another, 'Write to my wife regarding her divorce,' or said: 'Write to my slave regarding his emancipation.' Would that constitute a divorce or emancipation?"

Imam (as) replied: "There is no divorce nor emancipation until it is spoken by the tongue or written by his own hand with the intention of divorce or emancipation. It must also be done with proper witnessing and at the right time while he is absent from his family."
